current_example.problem:
Find $y(t)$ if the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

$$
y'' +  6y = 2\sin {2t}, \quad y(0) = 0, \quad y'(0) = 2
$$

is given by

$$
s^2Y(s) - 2 +6 Y(s)  =  2\left(\dfrac{2}{s^2 + 4}\right).
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}Y(s)-2+6Y(s) & =2(\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+4}), \\ ({s}^{2}+6)Y(s) & =2+\frac{4}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ ({s}^{2}+6)Y(s) & =\frac{2{s}^{2}+12}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ ({s}^{2}+6)Y(s) & =\frac{2({s}^{2}+6)}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\}=\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}\{Y(s)\} & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+4}\} \\ y(t) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $y(t) =  \sin {2t}$ is the solution of the original differential equation.
